subtopics.title: India's CPI 2025 Performance
subtopics.summary: India ranked 91st out of 182 countries with a score of 39 out of 100 in CPI 2025. This is a modest improvement from its 96th rank in 2024, but the score remains below the global average of 42. The source attributes this to persistent governance and accountability challenges.
facts: India ranked 91st out of 182 countries in CPI 2025.
India scored 39 out of 100 in CPI 2025.
India's rank was a modest improvement from 96th in 2024.
India's score remains below the global average of 42.
The booklet links India's position to persistent governance and accountability challenges.
India performs better than Pakistan, Bangladesh, Nepal and Sri Lanka.
India lags behind countries such as Bhutan and China.

subtopics.title: International Efforts and Bodies
subtopics.summary: UNCAC 2003 is the only legally binding universal anti-corruption instrument, and India ratified it in 2011. The FATF, set up by the G7 in 1989, acts as a watchdog on money laundering and terrorist financing. INTERPOL, established in 1923, is the world's largest international police organisation, and SDG 16 recognises anti-corruption as an institutional principle.
facts: UN Convention against Corruption 2003 is the only legally binding universal anti-corruption instrument.
G20 Anti-Corruption Working Group (2010) shares effective strategies to combat corruption, especially through emerging technologies.
Financial Action Task Force was established in 1989 by the G7.
FATF has 38 member countries and 2 member organisations: the Gulf Cooperation Council and the European Union.
FATF Black List labels Iran, North Korea and Myanmar as Non-Cooperative Countries or Territories.
SDG 16 acknowledges anti-corruption as an institutional principle.
INTERPOL was established in 1923 and has 196 member countries, including India.
INTERPOL's General Assembly is its highest decision-making body, with one delegate from each member nation.
